info.title: LocalRun — rebuild and run only what matters locally: scan repositories,
info.description: Try a library change in the services that consume it as a NuGet package, across repositories: lrun scans them, builds the project dependency graph, repacks the libraries in between into a local feed in dependency order, and runs the executables side by side.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: track dependency graphs and repack components to a local NuGet source.

commands.name: build
commands.description: Scan a directory tree for projects and write their dependency graph to a config file.

options.name: --root
options.description:
Directory to scan (default: your settings, else current directory).
Directory to scan, as for build (default: your settings, else current directory).
verify [options]
Check that the local feed holds an up-to-date package of every library of a config: none is missing, none older
than its csproj version or than a file of its folder. Exit code 6 if not.
Directory to check, as for build (default: settings, else current directory).

options.name: --local-nuget
options.description:
Local NuGet feed to repack into (default: your settings, else ~/.localnuget).
Local feed to check, as for build (default: settings, else ~/.localnuget).
schema <name>
Print the JSON Schema of a file LocalRun reads or writes, to validate or generate it: the config written by build,
the plan written by pack, the --json document, or the settings.
<name>: config | repack | result | settings
changelog [options]
Print what changed in each release of lrun, newest first, from the changelog shipped with it (no network). A local
build shows its unreleased changes too. With --json, each release's entries by kind, breaking ones marked.

options.name: --config
options.description:
Config file to write (default: .lrun/localrun.config.json).
Config file to read (default: .lrun/localrun.config.json).
status [options]
Print what a config holds, from the files alone (no scan, no NuGet source, no git): when and how build made it
(flags, lrun version, each repository's commit), its projects by solution and type with their versions, what was
left out and why, the repack plan if any, and the up running with it. Warns when the plan is older than the
config.
Config the up was started with: it records itself next to it (default:
.lrun/localrun.config.json).
settings [options]
Create your settings file if missing (all commented out), check it (warning settings-invalid), then open it. It
holds what differs from one user to the next: the local NuGet feed, the root to scan, the default suffix, how long
up waits after Ctrl+C before killing the processes, the log level. An option given on the command line always wins
over it.

options.name: --users-of
options.description: Keep the given projects and all that depend on them, transitively.

options.name: --deps-of
options.description:
Keep the given projects and all they depend on, transitively. With --users-of too: only
the projects between them (AND).

options.name: --git-changes
options.description:
Add the projects with uncommitted changes or commits not on origin's default branch to
--users-of (compares with your last fetch).

options.name: --union
options.description: With --users-of and --deps-of: users of one OR deps of the other.

options.name: --with-services
options.description: Also keep the executables using any kept project, with the libraries in between.

options.name: --include-external
options.description: Keep dependencies on projects that no solution references.

options.name: --tests
options.description: Keep the test projects (left out by default).

options.name: --csproj
options.description:
Read the csproj files as they are: don't ask MSBuild for versions and package ids set
elsewhere (props files, $(...)), and don't query your NuGet sources and local feed for
the latest versions (pack then starts from the csproj versions).

options.name: --plot
options.description:
Then plot the graph, as 'plot' does with its defaults, and open it (only on a terminal:
with output redirected, the page is just written).

options.name: --verify
options.description:
Then check the local feed against the config just written, as 'verify' does.
list [options]
Print the projects 'build' would keep, with their depth, type, version and solution, without writing anything:
'list --users-of X' answers "what uses X?". Doesn't query your NuGet sources.

options.name: --repack-config
options.description:
Repack config file to read, if there is one (default: .lrun/repack.config.json).
plot [options]
Render the dependency graph of a config file as an interactive HTML page: projects framed by solution, collapsible
into the solution graph, hover or click for users-of / deps-of.
Repack config file to write (default: .lrun/repack.config.json).
Repack config file to read (default: .lrun/repack.config.json).
up [options]
Build the executables of a config file, then run them side by side; Ctrl+C (or 'down' from another shell) stops
them all, killing what still runs after a grace period (--stop-timeout). Each one's output also goes to
<logs>/<name>.log. One up per config folder: a second one is refused (up-running). With --json, stdout gets one
line per event (building, started, running, stopping, exited), then the result on one line.

options.name: --output
options.description: Output path without extension (default: .lrun/plots/dependencies-<date-time>).

options.name: --open
options.description:
Open the page with the default browser.
pack [options]
Plan what will be repacked and to which versions, write the plan to a repack config, then pack in dependency order
into the local NuGet feed, as 'go' does.

options.name: --major
options.description: Increment major version (resets minor/patch).

options.name: --minor
options.description: Increment minor version (resets patch).

options.name: --patch
options.description: Increment patch version.

options.name: --next
options.description: Continue a prerelease (1.5.0-alpha.9 -> 1.5.0-alpha.10), or patch a release.

options.name: --alpha
options.description: Shorthand for --next --suffix alpha.

options.name: --suffix
options.description:
Set the prerelease label, without the dash (default: your settings, else local; e.g.,
'dev', 'beta.2'). An iteration number follows it: 1.4.3-dev.1, then .2 when packed
again.

options.name: --clean
options.description: Clean projects before restoring them.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description:
Only write the plan and print what would run; 'go' runs it later.
go [options]
Pack projects in dependency order into the local NuGet feed, following a repack config (from 'pack --dry-run',
possibly edited by hand).

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Executables not to run, e.g. the one you debug from your IDE.

options.name: --only
options.description: Executables to run, the config's others left out (combines with --exclude).

options.name: --logs
options.description: Folder of the services' log files, overwritten each run (default: .lrun/logs).

options.name: --stop-timeout
options.description:
Seconds to wait after Ctrl+C before killing what still runs, 0 or more (default: your
settings, else 10).
down [options]
Stop the up started with a config, from another shell or process, as Ctrl+C in its console would (grace period,
then kills), and wait until it has exited. Without one running, there is nothing to stop. Windows only.

options.name: --path
options.description:
Only print where the file is, and check it (default: ~/.lrun/settings.json, or
$LOCALRUN_SETTINGS).
doctor [options]
Check the setup before running anything: dotnet SDK, settings file, root, local feed (writable), every NuGet
source the projects restore from (reachable), and in each git repository origin's default branch and the last
fetch (--git-changes compares with it). Exit code 1 if a check fails.

options.name: --since
options.description:
Only the releases after this one, e.g. the version your scripts or an agent's
instructions were written for.
help [options] (also --help, -h)
Show this help message. With --json, the commands, options, exit codes, error codes and diagnostic codes as data,
and the agent instructions.

options.name: --agent
options.description:
Print instructions to paste into an agent's (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md...): how to drive
lrun, stamped with this version, and how to update them after an upgrade.
version (also --version)
Show the installed version. Please include it when reporting an issue.

options.name: --json
options.description:
Write one JSON document on stdout (result, warnings and errors, files written), even
when it fails; the logs go to stderr, plain.

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Fail (exit code 5) when the result left something out or may have a wrong version: name
collisions, cycles, MSBuild or NuGet source failures... The files are written all the
same.

options.name: --log-level
options.description:
Least important logs to print: Trace, Debug, Information, Warning, Error, Critical, None
(default: your settings, else Information). Debug adds timings and the stack trace of a
failure.
